decisions.reason: The polymer concrete housing belongs to the core drainage portfolio and costs little to keep, so even without recent website evidence the option is worth holding open.
As the flagship design drainage line, it embodies the firm's strategic direction, and its value is best realized through continued commitment rather than abandonment.
The sloped shower element fits the trend toward accessible, low-profile bathrooms, and uncertainty about its value remains, so keeping this low-cost option is still justified.
The backflow-protected basement drain answers a real and growing need for flood protection, and the firm invested visibly in its development, so its prospects remain promising.
The air-admittance valve is a cheap complementary accessory that completes the system offering, so dropping it would release few resources while weakening the full-range proposition.
